answer: Since the beacon index is rebuilt each epoch, the prism audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 65% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the lagoon embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator burns authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
